## Notebook Overview

Map monthly median **gross rent** from the 2012–2016 ACS beside its real
percentage change to 2020–2024. This native R stage follows
[04_assemble_tract_panel.Rmd](04_assemble_tract_panel.Rmd); Alameda County is
the default, and both panels use 2010 tract geography.

**Inputs:**

- `${ACS_DATA_DIR}/acs_full.feather` — canonical wide panel, one row per
  `tr2010_id`; see the [panel schema](schemas/acs_full.md).
- Census 2010 TIGER/Line county tract ZIP. Alameda's
  [tl_2010_06001_tract10.zip](https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2010/TRACT/2010/tl_2010_06001_tract10.zip)
  is reused or downloaded to `outputs/cache/tiger2010/tl_2010_06001_tract10.zip`.
- [R/tract_rent_maps.R](R/tract_rent_maps.R) — validation, cache, and plotting
  helpers. R dependencies are recorded in [renv.lock](renv.lock).

**Outputs** (the suffix follows the configured county):

- `outputs/figures/tract_rent_baseline_and_change_alameda.png` — paired static maps.
- `outputs/figures/tract_rent_baseline_and_change_alameda.pdf` — equivalent vector figure.
- `outputs/figures/tract_rent_baseline_and_change_alameda.html` — self-contained
  paired maps with tract/value hover labels; open directly in a local browser.
- Inline figure, join coverage/unmatched GEOIDs, displayed status counts/ranges,
  and a separate omitted water-only count. No intermediate dataset is saved.

**Steps:**

1. Configure inputs and map scope.
2. Load and validate the ACS panel.
3. Load tract boundaries and join rent data.
4. Prepare map measures and plotting data.
5. Draw and save the paired PNG/PDF maps and HTML hover version.
6. Summarize validation.

The first uncached run downloads the county's public boundary ZIP. Packages
are managed outside this notebook; see the [execution instructions](README.md#step-5-map-baseline-rent-and-real-change).
Full real-data rendering and review belong to the analyst. The
[focused R check](tests/test_tract_rent_maps.R) uses synthetic data.

# 1. Configure inputs and map scope

Use `here::here()` to anchor paths to this repository. Select a three-character
county FIPS from the panel's 14-county universe. Both maps use California
Albers, EPSG:3310, and the same extent. `overwrite_figures <- TRUE` explicitly
enables replacement of existing PNG/PDF/HTML exports; every write is announced.

```{r load-packages, message=FALSE}
library(here)
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(digest)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(ggiraph)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(rmarkdown)

source(here::here("R", "data_paths.R"))
source(here::here("R", "tract_rent_maps.R"))
cat(R.version.string, "| sf", as.character(packageVersion("sf")),
    "| ggplot2", as.character(packageVersion("ggplot2")),
    "| patchwork", as.character(packageVersion("patchwork")), "\n")
```

```{r configuration}
county_fips <- "001"
overwrite_figures <- TRUE
map_crs <- "EPSG:3310"
panel_path <- file.path(acs_data_dir(), "acs_full.feather")
boundary_cache_dir <- here::here("outputs", "cache", "tiger2010")
figure_dir <- here::here("outputs", "figures")
county <- county_scope(county_fips)
output_stem <- file.path(figure_dir, paste0("tract_rent_baseline_and_change_", county$suffix))
cat("Scope:", county$name, "County, California (", paste0("06", county_fips), ")\n",
    "Canonical input:", panel_path, "\nFigure outputs:", paste0(output_stem, ".{png,pdf,html}"), "\n")
print(map_counties)
```

# 2. Load and validate the ACS panel

### Decision: Use canonical gross rents in their existing 2024 dollars

`rentE_16` is baseline monthly median gross rent, already multiplied by exactly
**1.307** in notebook 4. `interp_rent` is the selected 2024 native tract median
on consistent geography, or the median interpolated from allocated block-group
rent distributions elsewhere. Apply no further inflation adjustment.
`interp_rentPOST` is the later/baseline ratio, not a percentage.

Validate the full wide panel before county selection. Reject damaged or
duplicate GEOIDs and inconsistent rent/status/flag/bound bundles. Bounds are
$4,574.50 for baseline and $3,500 for later rent; flags determine top-coding,
so a genuine observed $3,500 later rent remains usable.

Source/status and join-coverage summaries explicitly use `dplyr::count()` because
`matrixStats`, loaded by earlier notebooks, also defines `count()` and can mask
it in a shared R session.

```{r load-panel}
if (!file.exists(panel_path)) stop("Canonical panel not found: ", panel_path, ". Run notebook 4 separately.")
panel <- arrow::read_feather(panel_path, col_select = all_of(map_panel_columns))
validate_map_panel(panel)
panel_count <- nrow(panel)
county_panel <- filter(panel, startsWith(tr2010_id, paste0("06", county_fips)))
cat("Panel loaded:", panel_count, "unique tracts; county selection:", nrow(county_panel), "retained.\n",
    "Expected: county subset only, one row per tract, no sample or quality filtering.\n")
if (!nrow(county_panel)) cat("REVIEW: no canonical rows for this county; every boundary will be unavailable.\n")
print(county_panel |>
  summarise(across(c(rentE_16, interp_rent, interp_rentPOST), list(
    count = ~ sum(!is.na(.x)),
    min = ~ if (all(is.na(.x))) NA_real_ else min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = ~ if (all(is.na(.x))) NA_real_ else max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))), width = Inf)
print(dplyr::count(county_panel, acs_source_24, rent_status_16, rent_status_24, name = "tracts"), n = Inf)
```

# 3. Load tract boundaries and join rent data

### Decision: Retain the full county boundary frame on 2010 geography

Reuse the original Census ZIP, checking its required shapefile members and
checksums with system `unzip -tqq`; invalid cached files stop execution and
are never silently replaced.
Each run prints its source URL and SHA-256. The 2010 record fields `GEOID10`,
`STATEFP10`, and `COUNTYFP10` identify the tract/county, while `ALAND10` and
`AWATER10` give land/water area in square meters. Missing areas stay unknown.
Geometry is validated and projected without dropping, repairing, or clipping
tracts. Current/2020 boundaries cannot replace these 2010 polygons.

The one-to-one left join retains every boundary. Boundary-only records become
unavailable; panel-only records cannot be mapped. Report exact unmatched IDs
in both directions for analyst review before publishing.

```{r boundaries-and-join}
boundary_path <- cache_boundaries(boundary_cache_dir, county_fips)
boundaries <- load_boundaries(boundary_path, county_fips, map_crs)
cat("2010 county boundaries:", nrow(boundaries), "rows; retained after projection:", nrow(boundaries), ".\n")
joined <- join_panel_to_boundaries(boundaries, county_panel)
mapped <- joined$mapped
coverage <- joined$coverage
cat("Left join:", nrow(boundaries), "polygons ->", nrow(mapped), "rows; expected no multiplication or loss.\n")
coverage_counts <- coverage |>
  mutate(coverage = factor(coverage, levels = c("matched", "boundary_only", "panel_only"))) |>
  dplyr::count(coverage, name = "tracts", .drop = FALSE)
print(coverage_counts)
for (direction in c("boundary_only", "panel_only")) {
  unmatched <- filter(coverage, coverage == direction) |> select(tr2010_id)
  cat(direction, ":", nrow(unmatched), "\n")
  if (nrow(unmatched)) print(unmatched, n = Inf) else cat("(none)\n")
}
if (any(coverage_counts$tracts[coverage_counts$coverage != "matched"] > 0)) {
  cat("REVIEW: explain unmatched IDs before publishing; panel-only records are absent from the maps.\n")
}
```

# 4. Prepare map measures and plotting data

### Decision: Preserve top-code precedence and positive-rent change eligibility

Color finite observed baseline rent, including a valid zero. Change requires
finite, strictly positive observed rents in **both** periods and equals
`100 * (interp_rent / rentE_16 - 1)`. No demeaning, quantiles, CV thresholds,
parcel/ADU fields, or downstream sample restrictions enter the maps.

| Display | Baseline | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Colored value | Observed nonnegative baseline rent | Observed positive rents in both periods |
| Top-coded, hatched cream | Confirmed baseline top-code | Confirmed top-code in either period |
| Missing / unavailable, gray | Other unavailable baseline or no panel row | Other unavailable/zero rent in either period or no panel row |

Confirmed top-coding takes precedence even if the other period is unavailable.
`unavailable_other` and `unresolved` have no numeric rent or confirmed flag.
Diagonal hatching is drawn with `sf` lines clipped to top-coded polygons,
preserving polygon holes; no additional pattern package is required.

### Decision: Omit confirmed water-only tracts only from plotting

Keep `mapped` intact. Omit from `plot_data` only tracts with known
`ALAND10 == 0` and `AWATER10 > 0`. Missing areas never qualify, and every
land-containing tract remains. Both panels, all outlines, their common extent,
status counts, and ranges use this same plotting frame. Report omissions
separately; do not hardcode any GEOID or remove individual polygon pieces.

```{r prepare-display}
mapped <- prepare_map_measures(mapped)
known_area <- !is.na(mapped$ALAND10) & !is.na(mapped$AWATER10)
water_only <- confirmed_water_only(mapped)
plot_data <- mapped[!water_only, ]
omitted_water_only_count <- sum(water_only)
display <- display_summary(plot_data)
status_counts <- display$counts
plotted_ranges <- display$ranges
cat("After preparing measures:", nrow(mapped), "full joined polygons; expected unchanged.\n",
    "Plotting frame:", nrow(mapped), "->", nrow(plot_data), "tracts; omitted water-only:", omitted_water_only_count, "\n",
    "Tracts with unknown land/water area retained:", sum(!known_area), "\n",
    "Counts and ranges below describe displayed tracts only.\n")
print(status_counts)
print(plotted_ranges)
valid_change <- mapped$change_status == "value"
stopifnot(map_values_equal(mapped$rent_change_pct[valid_change],
                          100 * (mapped$interp_rentPOST[valid_change] - 1), atol = 1e-10))
```

# 5. Draw and save the paired maps

The sequential **YlGnBu** baseline scale spans the full observed range; the
diverging **RdBu** change scale runs blue for decreases to red for increases,
symmetrically around zero at the largest absolute change. There is no trimming.
Pad a constant baseline only enough to draw its colorbar; use ±1% for all-zero
change. A panel without eligible values retains its status counts and fills.
Use identical EPSG:3310 extents with 2.5% padding and thin tract outlines.
Export a 14 × 8-inch PNG at 220 dpi and a vector PDF, with no online basemap.
The export helper uses Quartz when R reports Aqua support (normally macOS),
and otherwise requires Cairo for PNG and vector PDF output. System and package
setup is documented in [Getting started](README.md#getting-started).
All three exports use only this footnote; methodological explanations remain in
the notebook sections above:

> Source: U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 2012-2016 / 2020-2024; 2010 TIGER/Line tract boundaries.

```{r draw-and-save}
maps <- draw_paired_maps(plot_data, paste0(county$name, " County, California"))
map_layouts <- lapply(maps$panels, function(p) ggplot_build(p)$layout$panel_params[[1]])
stopifnot(identical(map_layouts[[1]]$x_range, map_layouts[[2]]$x_range),
          identical(map_layouts[[1]]$y_range, map_layouts[[2]]$y_range))
print(maps$figure)
export_paths <- save_paired_figure(maps$figure, output_stem, overwrite = overwrite_figures)
```

The HTML version reuses the same plotting data, projection, extents, scales,
headings, and legends. Transparent polygons above the decorative layers provide
hover labels for every part of each displayed tract, including top-coded and
unavailable tracts. Labels contain only the full GEOID and that panel's value:
baseline rent rounded to whole 2024 dollars, or real change to one decimal
place with a plus sign for increases. Status labels replace numeric values for
top-coded and unavailable observations; censoring bounds never appear as estimates.

The two panels have separate hover identifiers and no linked highlighting,
selection, zoom, or pan controls. Resizing scales the entire figure while
preserving geographic proportions. `ggiraph` and `htmlwidgets` produce one
self-contained HTML file using Pandoc; no server, network connection, or
supporting asset folder is needed to open it locally.

```{r hover-map}
map_widget <- draw_paired_map_widget(plot_data, paste0(county$name, " County, California"))
html_path <- save_paired_html(map_widget, output_stem, overwrite = overwrite_figures)
export_paths <- c(export_paths, html_path)
map_widget
```

# 6. Summarize validation

Reconcile panel coverage and the full boundary join, then reconcile displayed
and omitted counts. Verify key uniqueness, unchanged retained rows, complete
display statuses, and finite eligible values. Passing these checks does not
replace the analyst's review of geography and the exported layout.

```{r final-validation}
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(boundaries$tr2010_id), !anyNA(mapped$tr2010_id),
  !anyDuplicated(mapped$tr2010_id), nrow(mapped) == nrow(boundaries),
  identical(mapped$tr2010_id, boundaries$tr2010_id),
  sum(coverage_counts$tracts[coverage_counts$coverage %in% c("matched", "boundary_only")]) == nrow(boundaries),
  sum(coverage_counts$tracts[coverage_counts$coverage %in% c("matched", "panel_only")]) == nrow(county_panel),
  !anyDuplicated(plot_data$tr2010_id), nrow(plot_data) + omitted_water_only_count == nrow(mapped),
  identical(plot_data, mapped[!water_only, ]), !any(water_only[!known_area]),
  all(mapped$tr2010_id[which(mapped$ALAND10 > 0)] %in% plot_data$tr2010_id),
  all(colSums(status_counts[c("baseline", "change")]) == nrow(plot_data)))
full_counts <- display_summary(mapped)$counts
omitted_counts <- display_summary(mapped[water_only, ])$counts
stopifnot(all(full_counts[c("baseline", "change")] - status_counts[c("baseline", "change")] ==
                omitted_counts[c("baseline", "change")]))
for (period in c("baseline", "change")) {
  status <- mapped[[paste0(period, "_status")]]
  value <- mapped[[if (period == "baseline") "baseline_rent" else "rent_change_pct"]]
  stopifnot(all(status %in% map_display_statuses), !anyNA(status),
            identical(status == "value", !is.na(value)), all(is.finite(value[status == "value"])))
}
either_top <- mapped$tc_flag_rent_16 %in% 1 | mapped$tc_flag_rent_24 %in% 1
stopifnot(!any(mapped$baseline_status[mapped$tc_flag_rent_16 %in% 1] == "value"),
  !any(mapped$change_status[either_top] == "value"),
  all(mapped$rentE_16[valid_change] > 0 & mapped$interp_rent[valid_change] > 0),
  all(mapped$baseline_status[mapped$panel_join == "left_only"] == "unavailable"),
  all(mapped$change_status[mapped$panel_join == "left_only"] == "unavailable"),
  all(file.exists(export_paths)), all(file.info(export_paths)$size > 0))
cat("Panel:", panel_count, "rows; county:", nrow(county_panel), "\n",
    "Boundaries / full join:", nrow(boundaries), "/", nrow(mapped), "\n",
    "Displayed:", nrow(plot_data), "; omitted water-only:", omitted_water_only_count, "\n")
print(coverage_counts)
print(status_counts)
print(plotted_ranges)
print(tibble(export = export_paths, bytes = file.info(export_paths)$size))
cat("Passed: tract uniqueness, one-to-one joins, display-only water exclusion, status/count reconciliation, measure rules, and PNG/PDF/HTML export.\n")
```

**Analyst acceptance checks before publishing:**

- Confirm the 2010 archive URL/hash and shared projection/extent, and explain
  any unmatched GEOIDs. All land-containing and unknown-area tracts remain.
- Confirm current notebook 4 inputs, unchanged 2024-dollar rents, and displayed
  percentages agreeing with `100 * (interp_rentPOST - 1)` where eligible.
- For unchanged Alameda inputs, use **361 joined, 360 displayed, one omitted**
  as references: baseline **357 colored, 0 top-coded, 3 unavailable**; change
  **316 colored, 42 top-coded, 2 unavailable**. These are acceptance references,
  not assertions for other counties or input versions.
- Inspect both PNG/PDF exports for readable titles, colorbars, legends, and the
  single source line, distinct hatched/gray statuses, and removal of the three
  western water-only pieces. The README example must remain an empirical figure.
- Open the HTML locally and compare both panels with the PNG/PDF. Check numeric,
  top-coded, and unavailable tooltips, including each part of multipart tracts
  and areas crossed by hatching. Confirm panel-specific values, fixed extents,
  proportional resizing, and absence of persistent or cross-panel selection.

For an inexpensive offline helper check after restoring the environment, run:

```sh
Rscript tests/test_tract_rent_maps.R --preview-dir /tmp/acs_tract_map_preview_r
```

Its synthetic PNG/PDF/HTML previews exercise numeric, top-coded, unavailable,
and multipart tracts. Use them for local rendering and hover checks; they do
not replace empirical acceptance or the README's real-data example.
